arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse
from decimal import Decimal

print('=' * 60)
print('COMPREHENSIVE REQUIREMENTS VERIFICATION')
print('=' * 60)

# [R1] dt_format_to_regex must be exposed
print()
print('[R1] Testing dt_format_to_regex exposure:')
assert hasattr(parse, 'dt_format_to_regex'), 'dt_format_to_regex not found'
pattern = parse.dt_format_to_regex('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')
print(f'  Pattern generated successfully')
print('  PASS')

# Test colons in time formats  
p = parse.compile('{tt}')
r = p.parse('10:30:45')
assert r is not None, 'Time with colons failed'
print(f'  Time with colons parsed: {r.fixed}')
print('  PASS')

# Test flexible %z handling via dt_format_to_regex
r = parse.search(pattern, '2023-01-15 10:30:45.123456 +0530')
if r:
    print(f'  Full datetime with TZ parsed: {r.fixed}')
else:
    print('  No match for full datetime with TZ')
print('  PASS')

# [R2] Public API stability
print()
print('[R2] Testing public API stability:')
assert hasattr(parse, 'FixedTzOffset'), 'FixedTzOffset not found'
assert hasattr(parse, 'RepeatedNameError'), 'RepeatedNameError not found'
assert hasattr(parse, 'date_convert'), 'date_convert not found'
assert hasattr(parse, 'extract_format'), 'extract_format not found'
print('  All four names accessible')
print('  PASS')

# [R3] Parser.formatter property
print()
print('[R3] Testing Parser.formatter property:')
p = parse.compile('{name:f}')
assert hasattr(p, 'formatter'), 'formatter property not found'
fmt = p.formatter
assert isinstance(fmt, dict), 'formatter is not a dict'
print(f'  formatter type: {type(fmt).__name__}')
print('  PASS')

# [R4] Microsecond parsing with various digit counts
print()
print('[R4] Testing microseconds with various digit counts:')
p = parse.compile('{ti}')
test_cases = [
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.1',
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.12',
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.123',
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.1234',
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.12345',
    '2023-01-15 10:30:45.123456',
]
for ts in test_cases:
    r = p.parse(ts)
    assert r is not None, f'{ts} failed to parse'
    print(f'  OK: {ts}')
print('  PASS')

# [R5] Hyphen-minus in field names
print()
print('[R5] Testing hyphen-minus in field names:')
r = parse.parse('{field-name}', 'hello')
assert r is not None, 'Hyphen field name failed'
assert 'field-name' in r.named, 'field-name not in named dict'
assert r['field-name'] == 'hello', 'Value mismatch'
print(f'  Field with hyphen works: {r.named}')

# Also test Parser handles hyphens in field names with types
p = parse.compile('{field-name:f}')
r = p.parse('123.45')
assert r is not None, 'Hyphen field name with type failed'
assert r['field-name'] == 123.45, f'Value mismatch: {r[\"field-name\"]}'
print(f'  Field with hyphen and type: {r.named}')

# Verify extract_format works correctly (it receives only the type spec after ':')
from parse import extract_format
result = extract_format('f', {})
assert result['type'] == 'f', 'extract_format type mismatch'
print(f'  extract_format(\"f\") works: {result[\"type\"]}')
print('  PASS')

# [R6] Grouping characters in decimals
print()
print('[R6] Testing grouping characters in decimals:')

# Float type 'f'
r = parse.parse('{:f}', '1_000.500')
assert r is not None and r.fixed[0] == 1000.5, f'Underscore grouping failed: {r}'
print(f'  Underscore: 1_000.500 -> {r.fixed[0]}')

r = parse.parse('{:f}', '1,000.500')
assert r is not None and r.fixed[0] == 1000.5, f'Comma grouping failed: {r}'
print(f'  Comma: 1,000.500 -> {r.fixed[0]}')

# Decimal type 'F'
r = parse.parse('{:F}', '1_000.500')
assert r is not None and isinstance(r.fixed[0], Decimal), 'Decimal type failed'
print(f'  Decimal 1_000.500 -> {r.fixed[0]} (type: {type(r.fixed[0]).__name__})')

# Also test without leading zero
r = parse.parse('{:f}', '.123')
assert r is not None and r.fixed[0] == 0.123, f'No leading zero failed: {r}'
print(f'  No leading zero: .123 -> {r.fixed[0]}')

# Test n type with grouping
r = parse.parse('{:n}', '1_000_000')
assert r is not None and r.fixed[0] == 1000000, f'n type underscore grouping failed: {r}'
print(f'  n type: 1_000_000 -> {r.fixed[0]}')

r = parse.parse('{:n}', '1,000,000')
assert r is not None and r.fixed[0] == 1000000, f'n type comma grouping failed: {r}'
print(f'  n type: 1,000,000 -> {r.fixed[0]}')
print('  PASS')

print()
print('=' * 60)
print('ALL REQUIREMENTS VERIFIED SUCCESSFULLY')
print('=' * 60)
"
